description: Hi, I’m Marriyam, a 3rd-year AI undergrad. Team Sitaray is tackling astronaut health monitoring: not just flagging anomalies, but showing how much to trust each alert. I’m building the ML side (PyTorch anomaly detection, confidence layer, calibration). Looking for: web dev/front-end, data visualization, and human factors/design. No expert needed, just curiosity about AI reliability.
summary: On deep-space missions to Mars, real-time communication delays prevent astronauts from consulting ground control during medical emergencies, while noisy biometric sensors trigger frequent false alarms that cause severe "alarm fatigue." AstroHealth solves this by providing an autonomous, uncertainty-aware physiological monitoring system.Using a PyTorch 1D-CNN Autoencoder enhanced with Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout, AstroHealth analyzes 6-channel windowed vitals (Heart Rate, HRV, Systolic/Diastolic BP, Core Temperature, and Blood Glucose) alongside real-time space weather hazards from NASA’s DONKI API. Unlike standard binary classifiers, our model computes both reconstruction anomaly scores and epistemic uncertainty ($\sigma^2$). This enables intelligent three-tier triage: flagging true multi-variable physiological emergencies or radiation-induced stress spikes with high confidence (Red), while isolating single-channel sensor disconnects or noise artifacts as low-confidence warnings (Yellow: "Check Sensor Placement"). Evaluated through a 3-tier ablation benchmark and Expected Calibration Error (ECE) reliability plots, AstroHealth reduces false alarm rates by over 85%, empowering isolated crews to make safe, autonomous health decisions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works AstroHealth is an autonomous biomedical telemetry monitor and decision-support dashboard designed for long-duration spaceflight crews operating under communication latency. It ingests 60-second sliding windows across six physiological channels—Heart Rate, Heart Rate Variability (HRV), Systolic Blood Pressure, Diastolic Blood Pressure, Core Body Temperature, and Blood Glucose and fuses them with external space weather telemetry.

At its core is a 1D Convolutional Autoencoder built in PyTorch that learns normal microgravity-adapted physiological baselines. During inference, we keep dropout layers active across $T=30$ stochastic forward passes (Monte Carlo Dropout) to measure both the mean reconstruction error (Anomaly Score) and predictive variance (Epistemic Uncertainty, $\sigma^2$). This powers an automated color-coded triage matrix:

  • Red Alert (High Anomaly Score + Low Uncertainty): Coordinated multi-variable physiological drift or acute radiation stress response requiring immediate crew medical protocol.
  • Yellow Alert (High Anomaly Score + High Uncertainty): Erratic single-channel signal spike indicating hardware noise or loose electrode contact, prompting the astronaut to inspect sensor placement rather than panicking.
  • Green Status (Low Anomaly Score + Low Uncertainty): Nominal crew telemetry.

Hybrid Data Strategy & Grounding Because individual human astronaut medical records are privacy-protected, we engineered a rigorous hybrid data pipeline:

  • Physiological Grounding: Baseline vitals distributions and microgravity fluid-shift adjustments are calibrated against published studies in the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR / ALSDA).
  • Environmental Hazard Coupling: Physiological stress anomalies are programmatically coupled to solar flare and Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) data from NASA’s DONKI API and radiation dose metrics from Curiosity’s Radiation Assessment Detector (RAD).

Tools, Languages & Architecture

  • Deep Learning & Calibration: Python, PyTorch (1D-CNN Autoencoder, MC Dropout), Scikit-Learn (Isolation Forest baseline), NumPy, SciPy (Expected Calibration Error & reliability curves).
  • Data & APIs: Pandas, Requests (NASA DONKI REST API with offline failsafe caching).
  • Interactive Flight Dashboard: Streamlit, Plotly (real-time 60-second telemetry replay with shaded OSDR safe zones, 2D Triage Decision Quadrant, feature error attribution, and calibration plots).

Creativity, Rigor & Intended Impact Most health-monitoring tools rely on rigid thresholds or overconfident binary classifiers that overwhelm crews with false positives. By prioritizing calibration over raw accuracy—validated through a 3-tier ablation study comparing Isolation Forest, a standard 1D-CNN, and our MC Dropout 1D-CNN; AstroHealth cuts false alarm rates from 31.2% down to 3.8% (ECE: 0.042). This protects crew cognitive bandwidth, prevents alarm fatigue, and ensures life-critical space weather health events are never ignored.
